emerging_technology: Model Context Protocol (MCP) and MCP server implementations exposing existing business capabilities to tool-using AI.
intended_application: Read-only internal product catalog, inventory, and public promotion lookup for staff in a small retailer; no customer profiling, purchases, or record changes.
organization: Hypothetical small retailer with an existing catalog application and a small IT team.
business_need: Reduce staff navigation across catalog and inventory systems and reuse tool integrations across AI applications.
users_stakeholders: Store staff, catalog managers, IT administrators, and customers indirectly affected by staff answers.
adoption_posture: Moderate/fast-follower; willing to trial an assistant on a limited read-only workflow.
capabilities_constraints: Existing catalog functionality is assumed; approved API availability, integration cost, and MCP compatibility are unverified. Small IT team and limited maintenance capacity.
risk_consequence_context: Stale inventory and incorrect public promotion answers; limited commercial disruption. This case excludes customer financial records and write actions.
management_question: How did MCP emerge from existing integration technologies and the needs of tool-using AI, and what does REST’s history suggest about the durability of MCP’s role in enterprise applications? What does the creation history imply for reusable catalog integration versus direct API calls in a small retailer?
time_horizon: Hypothetical 6–12-month pilot planning horizon with a 3-year integration maintenance perspective; not an adoption forecast.
additional_context: Analysis date: 2026-10-05. All organizational details beyond the user-supplied branch-banking workflow are explicit test assumptions. No customer records are provided.
